recap_subtitle: Welcome, hero! This is a quick review supported by programming examples and illustrations for each session you learned in the course to help you remember the concepts with ease and fun and prepare for the super exam! 🚀🌟

points.title: Python drawing library (Turtle)
points.desc: An excellent graphical library in Python for representing coordinates, movement of software objects, and drawing geometric shapes.

points.title: Draw mazes and move freely
points.desc: Programming the turtle to move forward, backward, and rotate at right angles to draw beautiful, precise geometric mazes.
points.code:
import turtle
t = turtle.Turtle()
t.forward(100)
t.left(90)
t.forward(50)
points.example: Drawing a 2D maze with turtle action step by step.

points.title: Reserve variables and interactive inputs
points.desc: Using the input function to receive texts and numbers from the user and store them in prepared software variables.

points.title: Calculate distances and multiply values
points.desc: Passing digital inputs typed by the user to dynamically direct the turtle's movement on the screen.
points.code:
steps = int(input("Enter the number of steps of the turtle: "))
t.forward(steps)
points.example: An application that asks the user about the side length of a square and draws it immediately.

points.title: Manipulating text strings
points.desc: Merge texts and change their code state to intelligently arrange and display welcome messages and outputs.

points.title: Drawing complex geometric shapes
points.desc: Draw complex stars and polygons at varying angles and color them based on the user's preferred text choices.
points.code:
color = input("Choose the color of the turtle (red, blue): ").strip().lower()
t.color(color)
points.example: Writing the student's name combined with colorful welcome phrases on the drawing board.

points.title: Logical conditions and decision making (If-Else)
points.desc: Instructing the program to execute custom code only when certain conditions are matched using reserved words if and else.

points.title: Programming the conditions for the direction of the turtle's movement
points.desc: Verifying the choice of travel direction (forward, left) and adjusting movement and angles based on the quality and safety of the condition.
points.example: An application that checks the air temperature and advises you to wear heavy clothes.

points.title: For Loops
points.desc: Repeating code execution a specified number of times using for and range to speed up programming tasks.

points.title: Drawing polygons and traffic light system
points.desc: Drawing regular geometric shapes (such as square and hexagon) and applying software to simulate an intelligent traffic light system.
points.example: Traffic light simulation application (red stop, yellow standby, green go) in Python.

points.title: Arrays and parallel iteration
points.desc: Passing and navigating through parallel data lists to calculate grades and total points for students in an automated format.

points.title: Turtle Race game
points.desc: Simulating a race of three colored strings moving at random distances, calculating the winning turtle and displaying an announcement of its victory.
points.code:
import random
distances = [random.randint(50, 150) for _ in range(3)]
winner = distances.index(max(distances))
points.example: A race of colored strings (red, blue, green) with a random win to calculate the odds.

points.title: Dictionaries
points.desc: An advanced data structure for keeping records and storing values ​​using distinct keys instead of numeric indexes.

points.title: Smart question bank and competitions application
points.desc: Use dictionaries to store questions and their model answers and check students' answers while calculating their total score.
points.example: Student control panel screen application to save his information, age, and favorite subject.

points.title: Recursion algorithms
points.desc: An intelligent and advanced technology in which the software function calls itself to solve complex and difficult problems step by step.

points.title: Drawing spirals and calculating the factorial (Factorial)
points.desc: Draw a cool geometric spiral, calculate the factorial of numbers (such as 5 factorial = 120), and program a simulation of a housekeeping robot.
points.example: A wonderful geometric spiral drawing that automatically decreases in size until the stopping condition is zero.

points.title: Debugging
points.desc: Developing the thinking of a professional developer through training in spotting spelling and logical errors and correcting indentations and punctuation marks.

points.title: Correct missing comparisons and symbols
points.desc: Corrected library typing, inserted missing commas and colons, and checked input conversion to numeric type.
points.code:
#Common error: age = input() ; if age > 10:
# Approved correction:
age = int(input("Enter your age: "))
if age > 10:
    print("You are over 10 years old!")
points.example: Fixed a broken engineering drawing script and restarted it with great success.

points.title: Managing dynamic lists
points.desc: Use advanced add, delete, and edit functions to manage student shopping lists and tasks efficiently and seamlessly.

points.title: Arranging and filtering software data
points.desc: Add new items to the array, sort them alphabetically or numerically, and delete completed records with an interactive click.
points.example: Interactive shopping list management app with automatic price ordering.

points.title: Ensure data integrity and handle exceptions
points.desc: Protect the program from sudden crash when entering text instead of numbers using efficient try and except blocks.

points.title: Verify that integers are entered
points.desc: Forcing the user to enter integer and positive numbers and repeat the question until the entered data matches 100%.
points.example: Secure the patient age receiving box to ensure the quality and consistency of record data.

sessions.session_title: Session 12: Capstone Project - Attendance & Report System

points.title: Super Capstone Project: Absence and Attendance Monitoring System
points.desc: Collecting all the concepts to build an integrated application that asks about the number of students, ensures the validity of the inputs, and monitors the attendance and absence of students dynamically.

points.title: Save attendance reports in real text files
points.desc: Writing a summary of monitoring absence, calculating it and the attendance rate, and storing the report in an external text file with the name of the updated day.
points.code:
import datetime
with open(f"attendance_{datetime.date.today()}.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write("Attendance and absence report for the day: " + str(datetime.date.today()))
points.example: Export and save a real text file containing attendance reports for the entire semester!
